# Dev-only containment, bundle hygiene and CLI parity verification

**Parent:** AH-0MVJUAADW0033QBD — Crash resilience: incremental telemetry upload so a mid-run reload loses at most one batch.
**Depends on:** AH-0MW6NI6BW003RJWH (end-to-end streaming) and AH-0MW6NJ3VU0038JHZ (exactly-once resilience).
**Slice:** delivery gate — proves the streamed protocol is dev-only, absent from a production bundle, opt-out clean, and transparent to the existing CLI tooling before the work item can reach `in_review`.

## Goal

As a **maintainer**, I want the streaming protocol to be provably dev-only and fully transparent to the existing dev CLI workflow, so shipping it cannot leak protocol strings into production or break `npm run record` / `capture` / `verify-dev-telemetry`.

## Scope

- **Bundle hygiene.** Extend `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` with forbidden markers for any new part-protocol string (marker header/flag name, `recordings/parts` path, run-key field) and confirm the dev-gated loader static-eliminates the streamer from `dist/`.
- **Opt-out.** With the share-telemetry setting off, assert zero part uploads and zero recordings (mirroring `verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`'s off-path assertion).
- **CLI parity.** `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` passes unchanged: one `session-*.jsonl` per run (parts never match the `session-*` glob), one evaluation artifact set, all `POST /api/telemetry/upload` responses 200, zero uploads/recordings when off. `scripts/record-session.mjs`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` and `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` behaviour unchanged.
- **Bounded-body check.** Confirm a run-end offline tail is skipped with the existing actionable line when it exceeds the 8 MiB CDP cap (no unbounded part bodies).
- **Full-suite gate.** Run the full project test suite through the test-skill runner (`/skill:test`) and confirm green, since the dev-push gate enforces it.
- **Tests.** Extend `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.test.*` (or equivalent), `src/telemetry/devModeEnforcement.test.ts` and `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts` for the new forbidden markers and the opt-out path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dev-only containment (parent AC6).** Streaming is behind the existing dev gate and is absent from a production bundle (bundle-hygiene markers updated for any new protocol strings); the opt-out setting produces zero part uploads — proven by the bundle-hygiene check and the opt-out test.
2. **Opt-out is clean.** With the share setting off there are zero part uploads and zero recordings written (parent AC6).
3. **CLI tooling is unchanged.** `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` passes without modification (one `session-*.jsonl`, one evaluation artifact set, all uploads 200, zero when off) and `record-session`, `capture-gameplay` and `inspect-telemetry` behave as before (parent AC3).
4. **Bounded tails.** A run-end tail beyond the 8 MiB CDP cap is skipped with the existing one-line actionable warning, never posted.
5. **Full suite (parent AC7).** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (via the test-skill runner; enforced at the dev-push gate).

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.mjs` — forbidden part-protocol markers.
- `scripts/check-bundle-hygiene.test.*` — marker coverage tests (if a test file exists; otherwise the enforcement scan test).
- `src/telemetry/devModeEnforcement.test.ts` — streamer static-elimination assertion.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneTelemetry.test.ts` — opt-out produces zero parts.
- `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` — runs unchanged (verification reference, not edited).
- `scripts/record-session.mjs`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — unchanged-behaviour reference.

## Notes

- Do not edit the CLI scripts to make parity pass; any needed edit signals a protocol leak and belongs back in child 3.
- This child is verification/containment, not new streaming behaviour; a failure here reopens child 2 or 3 rather than widening scope.
- Test runs go through `/skill:test` (test execution policy); infrastructure gates run their own commands.

## Intake questions for producer review

The Gym Index left column currently lists 16 plain scenes (AsteroidStress, BotTuning, Hangar, HexWar, Level, Minerals, Performance, Player, PowerUpLeveling, PowerUpsCombat, PowerUpsUtility, RechargeTuning, Rhythm, WeaponLeveling, WeaponTuning, Weapons), but the screen only fits ~9 rows (GAME_HEIGHT=540, startY=150, rowGap=42). The description proposes grouping into dropdowns. I need clarification on the grouping strategy and dropdown UX.

**Q1 — How should scenes be grouped into dropdowns?**

- (a) **By category** (recommended): Group by gameplay domain — Combat (Player, AsteroidStress, Level, Rhythm, Performance, HexWar, Hangar), Power-ups (PowerUpsCombat, PowerUpsUtility, PowerUpLeveling), Weapons (Weapons, WeaponLeveling, WeaponTuning), Tuning (BotTuning, RechargeTuning), Minerals.
- (b) **Alphabetical batches**: Split the sorted list into equal-size groups (e.g. 4-5 per dropdown).
- (c) **Manual grouping**: Producer provides an explicit grouping specification.
- **Recommended:** (a) by category — keeps related gyms together and matches how developers think about the gym library.

**Q2 — How should each dropdown behave visually and with keyboard navigation?**

- (a) **Expandable button per group** (recommended): Each group gets a single row with the group name and a down-arrow indicator; pressing Enter/Space or clicking expands it into its member rows below, indented or with a subtle visual cue. Collapsing hides them. Focus lands on the group header by default.
- (b) **Always-expanded with overflow scrolling**: Keep all rows but add vertical scrolling within the column (scroll wheel or Up/Down with wrapping at the column boundary).
- (c) **Pulldown menu**: A single click shows a traditional drop-down list below the button; the list disappears on click away.
- **Recommended:** (a) expandable group — preserves keyboard accessibility, fits the existing grid navigation model, and gives the developer control over what they need to see.

**Q3 — How should the ENEMIES and Dev Utilities columns behave with this change?**

- (a) **Same treatment** (recommended): Apply dropdown grouping to all three columns if any column overflows. ENEMIES is small (3 rows) so it stays flat; Dev Utilities (1 row) stays flat. Only the plain scenes column would use dropdowns in the current load.
- (b) **Only the plain scenes column**: Leave ENEMIES and Dev Utilities as-is since they never overflow.
- **Recommended:** (a) — build the grouping logic so it works for any column, even if only one column currently overflows. This future-proofs the design.

Please reply with your choices (e.g. "Q1: a, Q2: a, Q3: b") or your own preferred approach.
